human_summary: The 22 open systems were independently inspected against their printed crops, full-page crop-boundary overlays, skeletons, barline evidence and comparison layers. Their region counts and physical boundaries agree with the proposed frame, including repeat endings, separate pickups, key changes, measured Adagio transition and final bar. Essential musical notation is contained in the supplied crops. The four opening clefs and eighteen later piano-lower clef changes agree with the proposal, with cautionary glyph regions distinguished from their effective regions. Frozen system blocks were neither reconstructed nor reinspected; their supplied count summaries were used for cross-system continuity. Only indexed print images and nonsemantic geometry assistance were used; no reader, candidate, repair or previous review output was accessed. This submits an independent frame verdict for host validation and human sign-off; it does not publish or approve the piece.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Does the next section begin with a separately barred pickup?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. The bound frozen summary ends at P072; P073 is a distinct half-note pickup with two cello quarter notes, two-flat signatures and an opening repeat. No frozen block was recounted or reconstructed.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Are the endings and new repeated half distinct physical regions?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. P073 pairs with short first ending P081 or short second ending P082; P083 starts the next half and pairs with short first ending P097. Each repeat stroke group counts once. The second ending P098 includes the key cancellation, one sharp and Adagio transition and occupies a complete bar.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Does the Adagio transition retain a complete measured bar and closing barline?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. The bass has a quarter note, dotted eighth rest, sixteenth rest and half rest. The upper parts fill the same bar with the printed ornamental attacks and rests. The right double barline closes P098 before P099 on the next page.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Do the first and second endings remain distinct across system and page breaks?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. The first repeated span begins at P099, ends at first ending P106, and has short second ending P107. P108 is a separate half-note pickup; its short first ending is P116. Second ending P117 begins the next page as a complete bar, followed by the measured fermata close in P120–P121.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Are all later regions complete, including narrow bars and the final bar?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. P122 is a separate half-note pickup after the short P121 close. P123–P174 are full bars; the narrow P156 and P157 include the printed rests. P174 contains a half-note chord and half rest in piano, matching a full cut-time bar. The thin/thick final strokes form one boundary.

irregular_checks.where: System breaks in all open systems
irregular_checks.question_plain: Does any final bar lack a closing barline and continue as a split region?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: No. Each open system has its printed closing barline. Ties and slurs continuing over system breaks do not join the adjacent physical bars. The frozen counts remain bound facts.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Are all clef transitions and cautionary glyphs accounted for?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. Four opening clefs and eighteen later changes, all on piano lower, were independently checked. Six cautionary glyphs are in P074, P078, P092, P118, P119 and P162 and govern the next region. No C clefs or other changes are printed. Repeated unchanged system-opening clefs retain the current clef.
